Relative to self-supervised baselines, it raises top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1k from 42.2% to 67.6% for EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% for MobileNet-v3-Large.

author: Lynch
title: Transferring Knowledge Across Modalities: From Visual to Wearable Sensor Action Recognition via Distillation
abstract: Multi-modal strategies for human activity recognition (HAR) have demonstrated notable gains in recognition accuracy, yet the limited computational capacity of wearable platforms such as smartwatches prevents these methods from being deployed directly on such devices. To address this challenge, the proposed method presents an end-to-end distillation framework that transfers knowledge from a vision-based teacher to a sensor-based student. During inference, the framework requires only time-series accelerometer data from the wearable device, thereby reducing the computational burden on edge hardware while enabling the student model to closely approximate the accuracy of the more expensive multi-modal teacher. To preserve local temporal structure and make the data compatible with visual deep learning architectures, time-series signals are first transformed into two-dimensional images using a Gramian Angular Field (GAF) encoding scheme. ResNet18 serves as the teacher network, while a multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception is adopted as the student network. A novel loss function is introduced to reduce the cross-modal gap between the vision and sensor domains by jointly accounting for both distance and angular relationships among learned representations. Thorough evaluations conducted on the UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets confirm that the proposed framework is both effective and competitive, and is suitable for deployment on wearable sensors.

author: Hernandez
title: Bridging Neural Radiance Field and Neural Light Field via Distillation for Fast Novel View Synthesis
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Neural Radiance Field (NeRF)-based methods has demonstrated strong promise for representing intricate scenes using neural networks. A critical limitation of NeRF, however, is its impractical inference cost: producing a single pixel demands hundreds of queries to the NeRF network. Prior work addressing this limitation has largely focused on decreasing the number of sampled points along rays, yet the fundamental issue of iterative sampling remains unresolved. Neural Light Field (NeLF), by contrast, offers a more direct approach to novel view synthesis—each pixel is rendered through exactly one forward pass, entirely bypassing ray-marching. We propose a deep residual MLP architecture of 88 layers capable of effectively learning the light field representation. A central finding is that successfully training such a deep NeLF network requires abundant data, which we obtain by transferring knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model through data distillation. Evaluations conducted across both synthetic and real-world scenes demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms competing approaches. On synthetic scenes specifically, our method achieves a 26–35× reduction in FLOPs per camera ray alongside a 28–31× speedup in runtime, while also yielding substantially superior rendering quality—a 1.4–2.8 dB average PSNR improvement over NeRF—without requiring any customized parallelism.

author: Farmer
title: Knowledge Distillation for Computationally Efficient 3D Object Detection
abstract: Heavy computational demands remain a persistent bottleneck for state-of-the-art 3D detectors, even as the field has advanced considerably. We address this challenge by systematically investigating knowledge distillation (KD) as a means of building efficient 3D object detectors, with particular attention to pillar- and voxel-based architectures. Because established teacher-student pairs for 3D detection are largely absent, we begin by examining how to construct student models that strike favorable balances between accuracy and efficiency, considering both model compression and the reduction of input resolution. We then establish a benchmark that evaluates existing KD methods originating from the 2D detection domain when applied to 3D detection, covering six carefully designed teacher-student pairs. Building on these findings, the proposed method introduces an improved KD pipeline with two key contributions: an enhanced logit KD strategy that restricts distillation to a small number of critical spatial positions selected according to the teacher's classification responses, and a teacher-guided initialization scheme for the student that promotes the transfer of the teacher's feature extraction capability via weight inheritance. Comprehensive experiments on the Waymo dataset show that the proposed method's strongest configuration reaches 65.75% LEVEL 2 mAPH, exceeding its teacher model's accuracy while consuming only 44% of the teacher's FLOPs. The most computationally efficient configuration achieves 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, running 2.2× faster than PointPillar while attaining even higher accuracy. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD.

author: Ryan
title: Transferring knowledge via distillation from multi-modal segmentation networks to single-modality equivalents
abstract: Combining several imaging modalities has been an active area of research for medical image segmentation, with multi-modal information fusion consistently shown to yield higher segmentation accuracy than mono-modal approaches across a range of applications. In clinical practice, however, the simultaneous acquisition of multiple modalities is frequently impractical, constrained by scanner availability, the number of qualified clinicians, and the need to minimize cost and scanning duration. Consequently, a single modality is what is available in most real-world scenarios. We present a framework in which knowledge is transferred from a trained multi-modal teacher network to a mono-modal student network. The proposed method adapts the generalized distillation framework so that the student is trained using only one of the n modalities that constitute the teacher's input. We evaluate the proposed method on brain tumor segmentation using the BraTS 2018 dataset. Across multiple architectures, the student network is shown to consistently benefit from the teacher, outperforming a baseline mono-modal network in segmentation accuracy in every case.

author: Osborne
title: Knowledge Distillation from Deep Learning Models for Clinical Decision Support
abstract: Computational Phenotyping research faces both significant opportunities and pressing demands arising from the rapid expansion of Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR), particularly for uncovering meaningful, data-driven disease patterns and representations. Although Deep Learning models achieve superior, robust prediction performance on computational phenotyping tasks, their lack of model interpretability poses a critical barrier for clinicians who must rely on them in decision-making contexts. We present a knowledge-distillation framework, the proposed method, designed to produce interpretable phenotype features that simultaneously support robust prediction and replicate the behavior of deep learning models. Gradient Boosting Trees serve as the core mechanism within the proposed method for extracting interpretable features from deep learning architectures, specifically Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory models. Through exhaustive experiments conducted on a real-world clinical time-series dataset, the proposed method demonstrates performance that matches or exceeds that of the deep learning models from which knowledge is distilled, while additionally yielding interpretable phenotypes suitable for clinical decision making.

author: Moreno
title: Perception-Aware Agile Navigation Through Cluttered Environments via Privileged Imitation Learning
abstract: Neural control policies have recently surpassed model-based planning-and-control approaches for minimum-time autonomous quadrotor flight through cluttered environments. Nevertheless, these policies lack perception awareness — a property that is critical for vision-based navigation given a camera's constrained field of view and the inherently underactuated dynamics of a quadrotor. We introduce a learning-based framework that realizes perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. The proposed method integrates reinforcement learning (RL) with imitation learning through a privileged learning-by-cheating paradigm. A perception-aware teacher policy is first trained via RL using full-state information to achieve minimum-time flight through cluttered environments. Imitation learning is then employed to distill the teacher's knowledge into a vision-based student policy that relies solely on a camera to perceive the environment. By tightly coupling perception and control, the proposed method achieves a substantial gain in both computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate relative to existing approaches. Closed-loop control performance is validated through hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

author: Smith
title: Building Compact, Efficient, and High-Performing Domain-Specific Pretrained Language Models via Adaptation and Distillation
abstract: Many natural language processing tasks have seen remarkable gains from large pre-trained models; however, deploying such models within specialized domains introduces domain shift and creates significant obstacles for fine-tuning and real-time inference under latency and capacity constraints. We introduce a general framework in which off-the-shelf general pre-trained models are first adapted to a target domain and then subjected to task-agnostic knowledge distillation within that domain, yielding pre-trained models that are small, fast, and effective for domain-specific use. During the adaptation stage, the proposed method performs domain-specific vocabulary expansion, automatically determining the size of the incremental vocabulary using corpus-level token occurrence probability. We then conduct a systematic investigation of compression strategies for distilling large pre-trained models into compact domain-specific variants. Experiments carried out in the biomedical and computer science domains show that the proposed method outperforms BERT BASE on domain-specific tasks while being 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. Code and pre-trained models are publicly released at https://aka.ms/adalm.

author: Nguyen
title: Applying Knowledge Distillation to Compact Highway Network Acoustic Models
abstract: Over the past several years, deep learning has driven substantial gains in speech recognition performance. Yet neural network acoustic models tend to be far larger than conventional Gaussian mixture models, making deployment on embedded devices problematic. Our prior work introduced a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) — a depth-gated feedforward architecture — for acoustic modelling, demonstrating that HDNN-based acoustic models can match the recognition accuracy of plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models while requiring far fewer parameters. The present work extends this line of research by applying the knowledge distillation framework, commonly referred to as teacher-student training, whereby a cumbersome, high-accuracy model supervises the training of the compact HDNN. In addition, sequence training and speaker adaptation are examined within the teacher-student training setting. Using the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus as our experimental testbed, the proposed method yields substantial accuracy improvements for an HDNN acoustic model containing fewer than 0.8 million parameters, considerably closing the performance gap relative to a plain DNN with 30 million parameters.
